title: Magna Frisia
capsule: The Frisian Kingdom, sometimes styled Magna Frisia, was an early-medieval polity of the North Sea coastal lowlands stretching from the Rhine delta toward the Weser, controlling the lucrative trade emporium of Dorestad and resisting Frankish expansion across the late seventh and early eighth centuries. Its most powerful king, Redbad (r. c. 680–719), defeated Charles Martel near Cologne in 716 but lost southern Frisia after Pepin of Herstal's victory at Dorestad (689/690); on Redbad's death in 719 Charles Martel annexed the lands up to the Vlie. The kingdom's effective end came at the Battle of the Boarn in 734, where King Poppo (Bubo) was killed and the Frisian army was driven back across the Vlie, after which Frankish rule advanced; remaining eastern Frisian independence was extinguished only by Charlemagne's campaigns culminating in 772. (The later killing of the missionary Boniface at Dokkum in 754 occurred under Frankish overlordship, not as an act of an independent Frisian state.)
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The general territory is attested through Frankish annals and hagiographic sources, but precise Frisian borders at specific dates are speculative.
